categories.main_business_segments: Matador Resources Company operates two main business segments: (1) Exploration and Production (E&P) of oil and natural gas, primarily focused on unconventional shale plays, and (2) Midstream operations, which provide natural gas processing, oil transportation, gathering, and produced water disposal services, both for Matador and third parties through subsidiaries San Mateo and Pronto.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Matador leverages advanced horizontal drilling and multi-stage hydraulic fracturing technologies to develop oil and gas reserves, particularly in the Wolfcamp and Bone Spring formations of the Delaware Basin. The company also utilizes 3-D seismic imaging, real-time SCADA monitoring, vapor recovery units, and water recycling technologies to optimize production, reduce emissions, and manage water resources.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Matador's primary customers are unaffiliated purchasers, independent marketing companies, and midstream companies that buy crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs. The company also provides midstream services to third-party oil and gas producers in the Delaware Basin, with a significant portion of revenue concentrated among a few large purchasers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Matador's operations are concentrated in the United States, with a primary focus on the Delaware Basin in Southeast New Mexico and West Texas. The company also has assets in the Eagle Ford shale in South Texas and the Haynesville and Cotton Valley plays in Northwest Louisiana.
categories.supply_chain_position: Matador operates both upstream (exploration, development, and production of oil and gas) and midstream (gathering, processing, transportation, and disposal) segments. The company is vertically integrated in the Delaware Basin, controlling significant portions of the value chain from wellhead to market.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, Matador focuses on maximizing shareholder value through disciplined capital allocation, operational efficiency, and the development of unconventional shale resources. The company prioritizes drilling longer laterals, expanding midstream infrastructure, pursuing accretive acquisitions, and implementing ESG initiatives such as emissions reduction, water recycling, and safety improvements.
categories.revenue_model: Matador generates revenue primarily through the sale of produced crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs at market-based prices. Additional revenue streams include fixed-fee midstream services (gathering, processing, transportation, and disposal) provided to both Matador and third-party producers, as well as occasional asset sales and performance incentives from joint ventures.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Matador competes with major and independent oil and gas producers and midstream companies, particularly in the Permian Basin. Key competitors include larger, better-capitalized firms with greater resources. Matador positions itself as a technically proficient, operationally efficient, and financially disciplined independent with a strong presence in the Delaware Basin.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For 2022, Matador reported record oil and gas production of 38.5 million BOE (105,465 BOE/d), oil and gas revenues of $2.91 billion, and net income attributable to shareholders of $1.21 billion. The company achieved 22% year-over-year production growth, a 10% increase in proved reserves to 356.7 million BOE, and significant free cash flow, reflecting a robust growth trajectory and increasing scale.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Matador differentiates itself through its concentrated, high-quality asset base in the Delaware Basin, operational efficiency, technical expertise in unconventional resource development, and integrated midstream capabilities. The company emphasizes strong financial discipline, ESG leadership (notably in emissions and water management), and the ability to deliver consistent production growth and shareholder returns.
